correctness.rationale: The Kolmogorov forward equation yields F(s)=q/(q+mu)*(1-exp(-(q+mu)*(H-s))). Direct differentiation gives F'(s)=q exp(-(q+mu)t)[r B(q,mu,t)-1]. The stated exact identity B_t B-q B_q has three strictly positive exponential terms for t>0, so every interior derivative zero is a strict positive-to-negative crossing; endpoint signs prove existence and uniqueness and the two sharp rate regimes. The integral representation proves B>H and strict comparative statics. The boundary mu=0 is evaluated separately. The packaged independent numerical checker exercises 4498 assertions; no universal proof is attributed to computation.

originality.rationale: The exact claim is a complete, closed-form uniqueness/threshold theorem for a single patch created empty with its post-creation colonization rate fixed by previously appreciating funds. The indexed closest claims concern static recolonization allocations, survey timing, deterministic Allee rescue and other objectives; mathematical implication comparison found no direct coverage. Two fully accessible primary full texts were examined, Westphal was inspected in part, and a closely relevant inaccessible Southwell paper is explicitly identified as a genuine unverified historical-priority risk. There is no claim of proved worldwide novelty or exhaustive coverage.
residual_risks: A closely matching study by Southwell, Heard and McCarthy (DOI 10.1002/eap.1666) could contain a specialized result not observable from its abstract; its full primary text was unavailable.
Broader investment-timing, Markov decision, survival model, or optimal control literature could imply the theorem despite no indexed hit.
The result is restricted to exogenous independent colonization, constant exponential extinction and an exact fixed terminal objective.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves an interpretable baseline conservation finance and stochastic patch turnover scheduling problem for all positive colonization/extinction/horizon parameters. Its nontrivial one-crossing identity excludes local spurious optima and gives a computable sharp, strict comparative-static threshold. The extinction-driven region 1/B(a,mu,H)<r<=1/H makes delaying construction optimal where a no-extinction analogue prescribes immediate action; this exact boundary supports interpretation and benchmarking of larger restoration timing problems rather than an unsupported field prescription.
